scored.name: CarbideLoop (closed-loop tungsten carbide recovery)
scored.industry: Critical-material recycling from scrap: tungsten carbide and cobalt
scored.rung_one: An owned hard-scrap collection and grade-sort yard buying spent inserts, end mills and wear parts from roughly 20k US machine shops and regrinders via mailback boxes and routes, sorting every piece by grade (WC-Co ratio, Ta/Ti/Nb carbides, coatings) with XRF plus a vision/ML classifier, and selling assayed lots to US reclaimers and powder makers (Global Tungsten & Powders, Kennametal, Buffalo Tungsten, the DLA stockpile buyer) at about $2-6/kg over mixed scrap. Hard scrap trades around $25-40/kg W content; a 300-600 t/yr yard is about $10-20M revenue. Timing: the Commerce/DPAS rule in force since 27 Aug 2026 keeps tungsten scrap in the US, creating a domestic mixed-scrap glut, and DLA has an RFI for 200 t of hard scrap. GTP, Kennametal and H.C. Starck/Masan run brand-only take-back; brokers (Tungco) hand-sort; no ML-sorting startup found.
scored.ladder: 1) Sort yard and assay lab. 2) Owned zinc-process reclamation line (about $2-4M capex, permitting under 12 months) selling RTP powder to tool makers. 3) Chemical APT refining of soft scrap, sludge and low-grade lots. 4) Press-and-sinter blanks and rods. 5) Finished inserts and wear parts with buy-back, plus defense heavy-alloy feed. End state: a non-Chinese, mine-free tungsten chain (about $5-7B of tungsten value plus $25B of carbide tooling).
scored.software_layer: Rung 1: vision and XRF grade classifier trained on every piece, plus route and pricing engine knowing which shops generate which grades. Rung 2: grade-lot data set zinc-process recipes and predict powder properties. Rung 3: ML blend optimisation of mixed feeds against APT purity specs. Rung 4: sinter-process models on traceable feedstock. Rung 5: customer tool-life telemetry feeds grade design and buy-back pricing; the provenance-to-performance record of every kilogram is the asset.
scored.seed_plan: $1.5M: lease 10k sq ft in Ohio or Pennsylvania, buy handheld and benchtop XRF, build the conveyor vision sorter (about $250k), get a state scrap-dealer licence; sign 300 shops via regrinders in months 0-6, sell lots under offtake to two reclaimers and bid the DLA RFI in months 6-12, reaching about $6M annualised at 12-18% gross margin by month 18, then raise a Series A for the zinc line. Kills: tungsten price swings (back-to-back buys and sells) and the rule expiring Aug 2027 (defense demand is structural). Rubric estimate about 22/30: L1 5, L2 4, L3 4, L4 3, L5 4, L6 2.
scored.rung_one_economics: I could not check this live. The shared web-search budget was used up before my first query, and only one fetch (tungco.com) succeeded, so most numbers below are estimates from prior knowledge and are marked as such. Tungco does not publish its buying prices; sellers must request a quote. ESTIMATE: US hard carbide scrap traded at about $15-25/lb (about $33-55/kg gross) in 2025, and prices rose further after China's tungsten export controls (Feb 2025) pushed APT up sharply. The pitch's figure of $25-40/kg of W content looks plausible to low. ESTIMATE of the spread: the pitch claims $2-6/kg over mixed scrap, which is 5-15% of a $40-60/kg commodity. After buying, freight, mailback boxes, assay and working capital, that leaves the 8-15% gross margin the pitch itself admits (12-18%). A 300-600 t/yr yard at about $45/kg is about $13-27M revenue but only about $1.5-3.5M gross profit. Working capital is the binding constraint: 25 t of inventory at $45/kg is about $1.1M tied up, more than half of the $1.5M seed. Capex is light (lease, XRF at about $30-80k, sorter at about $250k claimed), so getting started is easy, but the business is a thin-margin, inventory-heavy broker. The zinc-process line ($2-4M claimed) is plausible as an ESTIMATE, but zinc reclamation tolerates mixed grades. That undercuts the main value of a grade-level ML sort: reclaimers already assay incoming lots and pay on W content.
scored.buyers: The buyers are capitalised and real. They are reclaimers and powder makers: Global Tungsten & Powders (Plansee group), Kennametal, H.C. Starck/Masan, Buffalo Tungsten, Sandvik/Wolfram, and Tungco (which also re-sells). Possibly also DLA Strategic Materials. The pitch's 200 t DLA hard-scrap RFI and the DPAS export-retention rule of Aug 2026 are UNVERIFIED (I could not check them) and should be confirmed before relying on them. Buyers are concentrated, about 5-6 of them, and they set price off APT/W content, so the sorter is a price-taker. Grade-sorted premiums matter mainly for direct-reuse or grade-specific feed, which is a smaller slice.
scored.incumbents: Rung one (collection and sorting of shop hard scrap) is crowded. Tungco (Madisonville KY, family-owned since 1969, self-described as one of the world's largest secondary tungsten suppliers, with plants in Ireland and Krefeld; source: tungco.com) runs nationwide buy programs. Kennametal, Sandvik Coromant, GTP and Iscar run take-back/buy-back programs that lock in the cleanest scrap from their own customers. There are many regional buyers and brokers (from prior knowledge, not verified this round: Carbide Processors, Federal Carbide, Huron Valley/others, plus numerous small dealers and eBay or online buyers posting per-lb prices). Regrinders, the pitch's planned channel, often already sell their scrap to these brokers. ESTIMATE: no ML-sorting startup is known, but the absence reflects low value from finer sorting, not an open niche. Funding: most players are private or family-held. Kennametal (about $2B revenue) and Sandvik (about SEK 120B) are large strategics.
scored.end_state: ESTIMATE: the global tungsten market is about $5-7B/yr of contained value, and the cemented carbide tool market is about $20-25B/yr (common industry estimates; not verified this round). The full chain is large and strategically hot (non-Chinese supply, defense heavy alloy). A path from scrap to APT to powder to inserts mirrors Kennametal or Sandvik vertical integration, but the later rungs are each capital- and know-how-heavy. Inserts in particular are a mature, brand- and application-engineering-driven market dominated by Sandvik, Kennametal, Iscar/IMC, Mitsubishi and Kyocera. The credible end state for a startup is a domestic RTP/APT recycler at about $100-500M revenue, not an end-to-end chain.
scored.killer: Commodity pricing, compounded by thin brokerage margins and a working-capital squeeze. Rung one earns a 5-15% spread on a volatile commodity (APT has swung by multiples since 2025) against incumbents with decades-long shop relationships and OEM buy-back programs that skim the cleanest scrap. The ML/XRF grade sort adds little value because zinc and chemical reclaimers pay on W content regardless of grade, so the data flywheel is weak. The timing tailwinds (the DPAS rule and the DLA RFI) are unverified and policy-dependent. The rule reportedly sunsets in Aug 2027, and a scrap glut caused by an export ban lowers the price a sorter can sell at, as well as its buying cost. Customer concentration is about 5 buyers. Later rungs (APT refining, sinter, inserts) each need $20-100M+ and process know-how held by Plansee, Sandvik and Kennametal.
scored.one_line_reason: Cheap and winnable to start, but rung one is a crowded, thin-margin carbide-scrap brokerage where ML grade sorting is worth little because reclaimers pay on W content. The real moat would come only at the capital-heavy APT and powder rungs, which incumbents already hold. Score 16/30.
